newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Union Texas led grp wins Venezuela Boqueron oil.
newsitem.headline: Union Texas led grp wins Venezuela Boqueron oil.

text.p: Union Texas Petroleum and Germany's Preussag Energie GmbH bid $174.78 million Friday for the contract to operate Venezuela's Boqueron oil field, state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) said.
The second highest bid was for $90 million by Agip, a unit of Italy's ENI, in association with Amerada Hess Corp of the United States.
Five companies or consortia bid for the field, the last of 20 to be offered this week in Venezuela's third auction round of operating licences.
Total bids for the week have topped the $2 billion mark.

The 60 square km Boqueron field, discovered in eastern Venezuela in 1989, was expected to attract strong interest. Currently pumping 8,000 barrels per day it is fundamentally an exploration block with no inactive wells.

Under the offered 20-year contract, the operator produces hydrocarbons on behalf of PDVSA subsidiary Lagoven in exchange for a fee worked out on a sliding scale. The operator must also invest at least $13 million within three years.

A total of 131 companies have competed for the 20 contracts offered this week with the winners determined purely by the size of their bids. Two fields attracted no bids, but PDVSA officials have said both would be re-offered.
